card.law_is_about: Stabilising statutory health insurance contributions and ending reimbursement for named complementary therapies.
card.they_claim: Swiss homeopathy has been a permanent insurance benefit since a 2005 HTA.
card.the_problem: Medical homeopathy coverage ended in 2005, returned provisionally in 2012 and became permanent in 2017.

claim_quote.translation_en: Translation: homeopathy has since been a permanent statutory insurance benefit.

counter_quote.original: Damit läuft die provisorische Leistungspflicht auf den 30.6.2005 aus.
counter_quote.translation_en: Translation: the provisional obligation to reimburse therefore expires on 30 June 2005.

locator.section: Krankenversicherung: Fünf komplementärmedizinische Leistungen werden nicht in die Grundversicherung aufgenommen

correction: For physician-provided homeopathy, Swiss basic-insurance coverage was suspended from 1 July 2005, restored provisionally in 2012 and made permanent in 2017. It was not continuously permanent from 2005.
effect: Weakens the claimed duration and continuity of the international reimbursement precedent.
limits: Swiss coverage exists today. The chronology correction does not establish clinical ineffectiveness or decide German reimbursement policy. Medicinal products have separate reimbursement rules; the claim is assessed as a statement about the medical method, consistent with the submission’s treatment focus.
context_and_alternatives: The immediately preceding clause dates a Swiss HTA to 2005 and asserts positive findings. The word seither naturally refers to that date. A conflation of current permanent status with the earlier evaluation is plausible. This finding does not adjudicate the differing 2005 HTA publications.
materiality_explanation: Minor: the historical precedent is overstated, while current Swiss coverage and the author’s other arguments remain.
direction_explanation: True: a longer uninterrupted reimbursement precedent strengthens the international example used to oppose removal in Germany; this is an argument-direction judgment, not intent.

card.they_claim: About 40 million euros a year equals 0.03% of GKV expenditure.
card.the_problem: Against the latest then-published annual total, it equals about 0.0114%.

claim_quote.translation_en: Translation: 40 million euros per year, 0.03% of statutory health insurance expenditure

counter_quote.original: Ausgaben in Höhe von 352,4 Milliarden Euro
counter_quote.translation_en: Translation: expenditure amounting to 352.4 billion euros

locator.paragraph: beginning Den Einnahmen der gesetzlichen Krankenkassen

correction: Using the 2025 preliminary expenditure total published on 10 March 2026: 40 million / 352.4 billion × 100 = 0.01135%, approximately 0.01%. A share of 0.03% would equal about 105.7 million euros on that denominator.
effect: Reduces the stated relative expenditure share; the small-budget argument survives and becomes numerically stronger.
limits: This checks the stated pairing, not the actual cost of all homeopathic care or the savings after substitution. The submission gives no expenditure base-year. Recent annual totals or the 2026 projection do not make 40 million equal 0.03%. A different numerator or older denominator could explain the percentage, but then the pairing needs qualification.
materiality_explanation: Minor: both the stated and corrected percentages are small relative to total GKV expenditure. The correction does not change the policy conclusion by itself.
direction_explanation: False: the erroneous percentage makes the stated expense look larger, which works against the author’s small-budget rationale.

sources.title: BMG, Finanzentwicklung der GKV im 1.–4. Quartal 2025, 10 March 2026
